problem.paragraph: For each predator-prey system, determine which of the variables, $$x$$ or $$y$$ , represents the prey population and which represents the predator population. Is the growth of the prey restricted just by the predators or by other factors as well? Do the predators feed only on the prey or do they have additional food sources? Explain.

list.item: $$\frac{\mathit{dx}}{\mathit{dt}} = - 0.05x + 0.0001xy$$ $$\frac{\mathit{dy}}{\mathit{dt}} = 0.1y - 0.005xy$$
$$\frac{\mathit{dx}}{\mathit{dt}} = 0.2x - 0.0002x^{2} - 0.006xy$$ $$\frac{\mathit{dy}}{\mathit{dt}} = - 0.015y + 0.00008xy$$

solution.paragraph: $$x = {predators}$$ , $$y = {prey}$$ ; growth is restricted only by predators, which feed only on prey.
$$x = {prey}$$ , $$y = {predators}$$ ; growth is restricted by carrying capacity and by predators, which feed only on prey.

problem.paragraph: Each system of differential equations is a model for two species that either compete for the same resources or cooperate for mutual benefit (flowering plants and insect pollinators, for instance). Decide whether each system describes competition or cooperation and explain why it is a reasonable model. (Ask yourself what effect an increase in one species has on the growth rate of the other.)

problem.paragraph: Lynx eat snowshoe hares and snowshoe hares eat woody plants like willows. Suppose that, in the absence of hares, the willow population will grow exponentially and the lynx population will decay exponentially. In the absence of lynx and willow, the hare population will decay exponentially. If $$L(t)$$ , $$H(t)$$ , and $$W(t)$$ represent the populations of these three species at time $$t$$ , write a system of differential equations as a model for their dynamics. If the constants in your equation are all positive, explain why you have used plus or minus signs.

exercises.instruction: 5–6 A phase trajectory is shown for populations of rabbits $$(R)$$ and foxes $$(F)$$ . Describe how each population changes as time goes by. Use your description to make a rough sketch of the graphs of $$R$$ and $$F$$ as functions of time.

problem.paragraph: 5. Details A phase trajectory is graphed on the R F coordinate plane. The horizontal axis (R) is displayed from 0 to 2000 in increments of 400 units. The vertical axis (F) axis is displayed from 0 to 300 in increments of 100 units. The phase trajectory forms a closed circular shape. The phase trajectory begins at a labeled point t = 0 (350, 100), goes down and to the right, concave up, and reaches approximately (800, 20). It then goes slightly up and to the right, concave up, and reaches approximately (2200, 40). It then changes direction, goes up and to the left, concave down, and reaches its extreme top approximately at (800, 320). It then goes down and to the left, concave down, reaches at t = 0, and completes the cycle. The rabbit population starts at about $$300$$ , increases to $$2400$$ , then decreases back to $$300$$ . The fox population starts at $$100$$ , decreases to about $$20$$ , increases to about $$315$$ , decreases to $$100$$ , and the cycle starts again.

list.item: The rabbit population starts at about $$300$$ , increases to $$2400$$ , then decreases back to $$300$$ . The fox population starts at $$100$$ , decreases to about $$20$$ , increases to about $$315$$ , decreases to $$100$$ , and the cycle starts again.

problem.paragraph: 6. Details A phase trajectory is graphed on the R F coordinate plane. The horizontal axis (R) is displayed from 0 to 1600 in increments of 400 units. The vertical axis (W) is displayed from 0 to 160 in increments of 40 units. The phase trajectory begins at a point (600, 160), labeled t = 0. It then goes down and to the left, concave down, and reaches an extreme on the left at approximately (100, 80). It then goes down and to the right, concave up, and reaches an extreme on the right at approximately (1800, 40). It then turns around, goes gradually up and to the left, concave down, and ends at approximately (950, 65).

exercises.instruction: 7–8 Graphs of populations of two species are shown. Use them to sketch the corresponding phase trajectory.

problem.paragraph: 7. Details Two curves are graphed on the t y coordinate plane. The horizontal axis (t) is displayed from 0 to 9 in increments of 1. The vertical axis (y) is displayed from 0 to 200 in increments of 50. The curve labeled species 1 begins at (0, 100), goes up and to the right, concaves up, reaches its high point at approximately (1, 250). It then goes down and to the right, concave down, reaches its low point at approximately (3.5, 45), and again goes up and to the right. It repeats the same pattern once more, and reaches the high point (6, 250) and the low point (8, 45). It exits the viewing window at the right of the graph at approximately (9.7, 70). The second curve is also graphed in the same coordinate plane. The curve begins at (0, 50), goes up and to the right, concaves up, reaches its high point at approximately (2, 190), goes down and to the right, concave down, reaches its low point at (5, 50), and again goes up and to the right. It repeats the same pattern once more, reaches the high point (7, 190) and the low point (9.7, 50), and exits the viewing window at the low point.

8. Details Two curves are graphed on the t y coordinate plane. The horizontal axis (t) is displayed from 0 to 15 in increments of 5 units. The vertical axis (y) is displayed from 0 to 1200 in increments of 100 units. The curve labeled species 1 begins at (0, 100), goes up and to the right, concaves up, reaches its high point at approximately (5, 1300). It then goes down and to the right, concave down, and reaches a low point at approximately (10, 1200). It then levels out and exits the graph at approximately (15, 1200). Find all the equilibrium solutions and explain their significance.

The figure shows the phase trajectory that starts at the point $$\left( {1000,40} \right)$$ . Describe what eventually happens to the rabbit and wolf populations. Details A phase trajectory is graphed on the R W coordinate plane. The vertical axis represents W and the horizontal axis represents R. The R axis is displayed from 800 to 1600 in increments of 200. The W axis is displayed from 40 to 70 in increments of 10. The phase trajectory forms a spiral shape. The phase trajectory begins at a point (1000, 40). It then goes up and to the right, concave up, and reaches an extreme on the right at approximately (1650, 54). It then goes up and to the left, concave down, and reaches an extreme on the top at approximately (1050, 80). It then goes down and to the left, concave down, and reaches an extreme on the left at approximately (850, 69). It then goes down and to the right, concave up, and reaches an extreme on the bottom at approximately (1000, 58). It follows the same trend once more and reaches its center at approximately (1000, 64).
Sketch graphs of the rabbit and wolf populations as functions of time.
$$W = 0$$ , $$R = 0$$ : Zero populations
$$W = 0$$ , $$R = 5000$$ : In the absence of wolves, the rabbit population is always $$5000$$ .
$$W = 64$$ , $$R = 1000$$ : Both populations are stable.

solution.paragraph: The populations stabilize at $$1000$$ rabbits and $$64$$ wolves.
